question.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(z)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-6{z}^{3}-12{z}^{2}+20z & =3{z}^{2}-16z \\ -6{z}^{3}-15{z}^{2}+20z & =-16z \\ -6{z}^{3}-15{z}^{2}+36z & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $-3z.$ We can factor out the $-3z$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-6{z}^{3}-15{z}^{2}+36z & =0 \\ -3z(2{z}^{2}+5z-12) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $2{z}^{2}+5z-12$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3z(2{z}^{2}+5z-12) & =0 \\ -3z(2z-3)(z+4) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $z=0,$ $z=\frac{3}{2},$ and $z=-4.$
